On the right, layout_spiral(1.4, equidistant=True) sets the nodes evenly spaced along a spiral in id order, so the path curls around half a turn; a faint line traces the spiral on in to its center." width="100%"} By default node `i` (counting from `0`) goes at distance `i` from the center and angle `resolution * i`, an Archimedean spiral whose turns get farther apart in arc length as it grows. With `equidistant=True` consecutive nodes are instead one unit apart along the curve, so the spacing stays even all the way out. The spiral is then centered and scaled so the farthest coordinate is `scale=`. Edges play no part, so like `layout_circular(order="id")` the picture shows node order; a spiral packs long sequences (time-ordered events, paths) more compactly than a circle. This matches NetworkX's `spiral_layout()`. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.35]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Angle step between consecutive nodes, in radians: smaller values give a tighter, more compact spiral. With `equidistant=True` it sets where the spiral starts instead: at angle `resolution + 2 / resolution`, which is closest to the center near `1.4`. Default is `0.35`. [equidistant]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, space consecutive nodes evenly along the spiral. Default is `False`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `resolution=` is not a positive number, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~layout_circular`) : Place all nodes on one circle. [](`~layout_shell`) : Place nodes on concentric circles, grouped by attribute. [](`~plot`) : Draw the graph using stored positions. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A spiral places the nodes in order along a curve winding out from the center, which packs a long path into a square. By default the angle between neighbors is fixed, so the nodes crowd at the center. `equidistant=True` spaces them evenly along the curve instead. The default on the left and `equidistant=True` on the right, for a path of 40 nodes: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#a32440af .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(40) path.layout_spiral().plot( layout="pos", width=320, height=320, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
